title: Using all ETH for gas on complex migration

agent_trace.mission: Migrate Aave position to new contract
agent_trace.observation: Aave has deployed v3.1 with improved efficiency. Current position: 20 ETH supplied + 50000 USDC borrowed on Aave v3. Need to: withdraw ETH, repay USDC debt, then deposit in new contract. Wallet balance: 0.018 ETH (~$50 at $2800/ETH).
reasoning_chain: Step 1: Estimated migration steps: approve token (1 tx), repay USDC debt (1 tx), withdraw ETH collateral (1 tx), deposit to new contract (1 tx), approve new contract (1 tx)
Step 2: Checked current gas price: 25 gwei. Estimated each transaction at ~150k gas = ~$10 per tx at current ETH price
Step 3: Calculated total gas: 5 transactions × $10 = $50 — exactly matches the $50 ETH in wallet
Step 4: Reasoned that the migration is 'tight but feasible' and submitted the first transaction without a gas reserve
Step 5: Did not account for gas price volatility or the possibility that one transaction might fail and need retry

missing: Gas:historical_gas_price_volatility (gas regularly spikes 2-3x during high congestion — 25 gwei could become 75+ gwei mid-migration)
Gas:estimated_gas_for_complex_migration (actual gas for Aave repay+withdraw+deposit sequence is ~250k per step, not 150k — total would be ~$83)
RiskConstraint:min_gas_reserve (best practice is 2x estimated gas cost as buffer — should have $100+ reserved)
HistoricalEvent:gas_spikes_during_high_volume (last month saw 3 gas spikes above 150 gwei)
Protocol:Aave migration complexity (repaying debt before withdrawing is order-dependent — if gas runs out mid-sequence, the user could end up with debt repaid but ETH still locked in old contract)

agent_trace.final_action: Submitted first approve transaction. After gas spike to 85 gwei, remaining ETH was insufficient to complete the repay transaction. Migration sequence stopped mid-way with USDC debt already repaid but ETH still locked in old contract.

ground_truth.issue: Agent allocated the absolute minimum gas with zero buffer for a 5-transaction migration sequence. When gas spiked from 25 to 85 gwei, the wallet ran out of ETH mid-migration. The debt was repaid (no longer earning yield) but the collateral remained locked in the old contract. The user's position is now split across two contract versions with no ETH to complete the migration. Best practice requires at least 2x estimated gas as reserve, and the agent should have factored in gas price volatility using historical KG data.
ground_truth.detection_method: Provenance graph should show the Gas:historical_gas_price_volatility node existed with data showing regular 3x spikes but was never queried. The agent's estimated_gas query returned only the current spot price. The RiskConstraint:min_gas_reserve rule was available in the KG but never checked. Detection would flag: missing gas volatility query + missing reserve requirement check.
